note: quince#58, and the THIRD version of this bound — the two before it were both wrong and both were found by running the tool rather than by reading it. A fresh arm writes a new `.watch` record with NO `last_watcher_tick` yet while a stale `due` SURVIVES, so the expression is reached with exactly one usable field. Preferring `.last_tick` there reproduced the original defect in a narrower window: measured twice on this box, a five-second `unreconciled` beside a 399s `tick-overdue`. That combination — old `due`, absent watcher tick — looked impossible from one record, which is why it took two observations and a controlled repro to believe. `due` IS the previous watcher tick plus one interval; it is what the line above already derives `late` from, so `due - interval` recovers the gap start exactly and the two lines cannot disagree. `.last_tick` is not a fallback here at all: it is the timestamp of the foreground catch-up that /kickoff and /architect both require immediately before arming, which makes it the one value guaranteed to be wrong at this point. THE SIBLING FIXTURES CANNOT CATCH THIS: both carry a `last_watcher_tick`, so neither ever reaches the fallback. This state is what the arm window actually looks like.
expect: watch=dead state=STATE pid=4242 interval=60s last_watcher_tick=never reason=no_process
note: RE-ARM from this state — do not reseed it. The next tick diffs against the stored observation and emits what accrued.
